newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says ship deaths have hastened Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Italy says ship deaths have hastened Albania force.

text.p: Italy said on Sunday that an international mission for Albania had been given greater impetus by the death of refugees from the Balkan country who drowned when their boat sank in the Adriatic.

"We need several days. The operation is complicated, involving taking control of ports in cooperation with regular Albanian forces," said Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini in an interview with the daily La Stampa newspaper.

Dini was asked whether the incident, in which a small harbour patrol boat crowded with Albanians sank on Friday night after colliding with a navy corvette trying to prevent it entering Italian waters, had speeded matters up.
"Absolutely, because illegal immigration is not something that concerns just Italy," he replied.

"Our community partners know full well that it affects them too. Together we are aiming at "stabilising" the population in Albanian territory, providing them with the physical security and conditions needed to allow them to stay."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday that the tragedy made the Italian-led mission, authorised by the U.N. Security Council, more urgent.
Four people are known to have died in Friday's shipwreck but some of the 34 rescued survivors said afterwards that many more people, mostly women and children, had drowned.
Italian newspapers gave a variety of estimates on Sunday, with some suggesting that as many as 100 had died.
The incident provoked Tirana's anger and came at a delicate time for Italy, prime mover of the force of police or troops intended to protect food and medical supplies in Albania.

Italy warned its nationals in southern Albania to limit their stays to the minimum time possible but newspapers quoted Albanian president Sali Berisha as assuring that the Italians would be well received in the country.

"I would like to reassure the families of soldiers coming to Albania that their sons and husbands will be arriving in a friendly country, where they will find a friendly people that appreciates their mission," he was quoted as saying.

The Italian navy said on Saturday that there was no hope of finding any more survivors but it was still searching for bodies. The navy's chief of staff told a news conference that he doubted the high figures given by survivors.

Dini said in a statement on Saturday night that the Rome government was unshaken in its determination to "provide every help to encourage the pacification and democratic development of Albania" through joint international action.
He told La Stampa on Sunday that the tragedy was an accident that could not have been easily avoided.
"Our navy had the task of stopping boats bringing illegal immigrants to Italy and the Albanian boat did not stop.
"It tried in every way to evade the two Italian ships and then, after several risky manouevres, set itself on a collision course with our vessel that could not avoid it."
Some of the refugees have been quoted as saying that the Italian ship bore down on them.
Two enquiries have been opened in Italy.

The captain of the Albanian boat survived and has been arrested while the commanding officer of the Italian ship, which has been placed under judicial sequestration as a matter of course, is to be questioned by magistrates.
Dini said that Italy was not denying anyone's right to asylum but most of the 13,000 Albanians who have flooded into the country in recent weeks were not real refugees.

"What is happening in Albania is the illegal immigration to Italy of people who do not need asylum and who are not seeking asylum. They merely want to cross the borders of the European Union in order to get work," he said.
"Our government's action is right, carefully thought out and balanced. And we have no intention of changing it."
